feature: A walk can check what a keyboard shortcut really does
summary: An unmanned walk can now press a real menu shortcut and fail loudly when it does not run. It also stops reporting a dead chord as a pass: pressing Command Z in a walk used to log "taken by menu" and change nothing, which read like undo working.
setup: Nothing to install. This is loop tooling, not app UI: run Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/undo-shortcut-walk.json and read /tmp/photonz-playtest/undo-shortcut/log.json.

try.do: In the log, find step 10: shift Command N reached File > New Window and it ran, a real shortcut pressed by an unmanned walk.
Find step 13: Command Z now says which item took it and that nothing was behind it, so nothing happened.
Compare the layer count at step 15 (still 2, the rectangle is there) with step 19 (1, undone by an action step).
Read the new "Which shortcuts a walk can press" section in docs/design/playtest-harness.md.
Write a step { "do": "shortcut", "key": "z", "modifiers": ["command"] } into any walk and watch it fail with the reason and the workaround.

evaluate: Is a shortcut step that only works for app-level chords worth having, or would you rather walks just never claim to check shortcuts?
Does the Command Z log line tell you enough to stop trusting it, without having to read the design doc?
The loop still never takes focus, so window shortcuts stay uncheckable. Is that the right trade, or is a foreground playtest mode worth building?
Should a walk fail outright when a key step lands on an item with nothing behind it, instead of only saying so?
rough: The headline ask was for a walk to press Command Z and show the edit undone. That is not possible and now has proof rather than a hunch: macOS refuses a script-launched background process focus, so NSApp.activate, makeKeyAndOrderFront and becomeKey all leave isActive false, with the window visible and hidden. Without a focus event SwiftUI never re-evaluates the menu bar, so every window-scoped item keeps a nil action for the whole walk and forcing it enabled changes nothing.
So a walk can prove undo WORKS (action undo, watch layers and canRedo) but cannot prove Command Z is wired to it. That last link still needs a person at the keyboard.
A first attempt gave the menu commands a stand-in editor for the walk. It was removed once the nil action turned up: it changed nothing and it put a test seam in shared release code for no gain.
Screen Recording was granted, so the shot above is a real screen capture of the probe, not an offscreen render.
